draft_subject: A civic-threshold question for an architect and a social scientist
draft_body:
Dear Social Science and Architecture Committee,

The committee’s recent urban-comfort discussion treats comfort as a condition for participation (https://www.aiany.org/committees/social-science-architecture-committee/). I’m looking for a similarly precise conversation about who can use a threshold when a service acts on someone’s behalf.

I’m preparing a PhD proposal for Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. A first case would compare a shared civic-building entrance with a separate proxy pickup bay. Personal arrival and staying remain available; the study would track access, detours, waiting, staff work and how people contest an expired instruction.

Could the committee suggest one architect and one social scientist who could critique this comparison? I would value a relevant public discussion or introduction before choosing a doctoral home.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer
Proxy Society
https://proxysociety.org/architecture

Your Contact Us page identifies Ask NYPL as the reference and support desk (https://www.nypl.org/get-help/contact-us). I’m seeking guidance on the appropriate route for an external architecture-research question, rather than collection access alone.

draft_body:
Dear North America PRS team,

The partnership’s public Practice Research Symposium model interests me as a way to examine spatial decisions through practice (https://www.newschool.edu/parsons/rmit-phd-design-partnership/). I understand that enrolment and the degree are at RMIT, with research based at Parsons.

I’m preparing a PhD proposal for Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. The design practice would compare a civic-building proxy handoff recess with a shared staffed threshold. Plans, sections, staged prototypes and film would test expiry, revocation, accessible passage and continued personal arrival.

Could you clarify whether this architectural enquiry fits the current practice-based pathway, and how lead RMIT and associate Parsons supervisors are matched? I would also appreciate current intake, eligibility and international NYC attendance requirements before preparing an application.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer
Proxy Society
